note.question: How should a financially distressed small business design advance sales so that strategic customers fund survival without creating excessive free riding or destroying the owner's incentive to deliver quality?
note.overview: A distressed firm, competitive bank, and continuum of forward-looking customers interact sequentially. Consumers strategically decide whether to buy early based on others' participation and the firm's anticipated price/effort, while firm moral hazard and bank break-even conditions determine a symmetric rational-expectations equilibrium.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In the financing period, the firm chooses an advance-selling contract and inner-circle consumers decide whether to participate; the resulting funds may be combined with a bank loan whose rate satisfies bank break-even. If financing succeeds and operations resume, the firm chooses unobservable effort and a regular price, demand realizes, consumers purchase, the bank is repaid subject to limited liability, and residual revenue becomes firm profit. Each infinitesimal consumer can free ride on others' support because her own refusal need not trigger bankruptcy. Selling service early reduces the firm's future marginal return to quality effort.
